name: Sudanese Ful Medames
description: Ful medames, slow-simmered fava beans mashed with garlic, lemon, and oil, is one of Sudan's most essential everyday dishes, eaten at nearly any meal.
steps_detailed: Simmer the fava beans with a splash of water, 8-10 minutes, until very soft.
Mash roughly, leaving some texture, and stir in the garlic, lemon juice, cumin, and olive oil.

name: Sudanese Kisra
description: Kisra, a thin, fermented sorghum flatbread, is Sudan's most essential staple bread, traditionally torn and used to scoop up stew - real sorghum flour isn't a distinct item here, so this leans on all-purpose flour for a similar thin flatbread shape.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, vinegar, and 1 cup water into a thin batter.
Let sit at room temperature 6-8 hours to develop some tang.
Pour a thin layer into a hot, lightly oiled non-stick pan and cook, covered, without flipping, 2-3 minutes, until set.

Let sit at room temperature 6-8 hours to develop some tang.

name: Sudanese Asida
description: Asida, a smooth sorghum or wheat porridge served with a well of stew or butter and honey, is a genuine Sudanese staple, especially for celebrations.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour into 1.5 cups boiling water and cook, stirring constantly, 10-12 minutes until thick and smooth.
Serve with a well of melted butter and honey poured over the top.

Scoop out the flesh and mash with the garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil.
